title: Finley — AI-Powered Financial Planning and Analysis for SMBs
content:
Finley is the AI financial analyst that every small business deserves. We automate the financial reporting, forecasting, and planning that used to require a full-time CFO or expensive consultants — making enterprise-grade financial intelligence accessible to businesses of every size.

Small and mid-size businesses run the economy but are chronically underserved by financial tools. Most still manage their finances in spreadsheets, spending hours each month on manual reporting and making critical decisions with incomplete data. Meanwhile, enterprise companies have entire FP&A teams and six-figure software budgets.

Finley levels the playing field. Connect your accounting software — QuickBooks, Xero, or FreshBooks — and your bank feeds, and Finley automatically categorizes transactions, generates financial reports, builds cash flow forecasts, and surfaces actionable insights. Our AI forecasting engine predicts revenue, expenses, and cash position with 92% accuracy on 90-day forecasts.

No more waiting until month-end close to understand your financial position. No more manually building board decks. No more guessing about cash runway. Finley gives you a real-time financial command center that updates continuously.

Founded in 2023 by Michael Chang, former Head of FP&A at Stripe, and Priya Anand, formerly a principal engineer at Plaid, Finley combines deep financial expertise with world-class data infrastructure. Our team of 26 in San Francisco serves over 320 SMB customers. Backed by Kleiner Perkins and Ribbit Capital.

title: Finley — First Meeting with Michael Chang (CEO)
author: Sarah Chen
content:
Meeting: Introduction — Finley
Date: February 5, 2026
Attendees: Sarah Chen (AIVC), Michael Chang (CEO, Finley)
Location: AIVC office, San Francisco

## Summary

Michael came recommended by our Kleiner Perkins contacts. Immediate good impression — sharp, articulate, and deeply knowledgeable about financial operations. His Stripe FP&A background is directly relevant.

## Key Discussion Points

- **Problem**: SMBs (1-200 employees) manage finances primarily in spreadsheets. They can't afford a full-time CFO or expensive FP&A software (Anaplan, Adaptive Insights run $50K+/year). This means financial decisions are made with stale data, manual reports, and gut instinct. Cash flow surprises are the #1 killer of small businesses.

- **Solution**: Finley connects to existing accounting software (QBO, Xero, FreshBooks) and bank feeds via Plaid integrations. It automatically categorizes transactions, generates financial reports (P&L, balance sheet, cash flow), builds forecasts using AI, and surfaces insights ("your burn rate increased 15% this month — here's why"). Think of it as an AI CFO.

- **Traction**: 320 SMB customers. $1.9M ARR. Average ACV $6K/year. Product-led growth: 15% monthly activation rate from free trial. Self-serve product — no sales team needed for most customers.

- **Team**: Michael Chang (CEO) was Head of FP&A at Stripe for 3 years — managed a $300M budget and a team of 25 analysts. Stanford MBA. Priya Anand (CTO) was a principal engineer at Plaid — built their bank data aggregation infrastructure. 26 employees, San Francisco.

- **Fundraise**: Series A, $12M total. Ribbit Capital is interested in co-leading — they want to put in $7M. Looking for a co-lead for $5M. $38M pre-money valuation. Kleiner Perkins following on with $1.5M.

## Ribbit Co-Lead

Ribbit's involvement is a strong signal. They're the premier fintech investor and their involvement gives Finley credibility with financial services partners and customers. Michael wants a co-lead who brings AI/tech expertise to complement Ribbit's fintech knowledge. AIVC fits that profile.

## My Assessment

The product-led growth motion is compelling — 15% trial-to-paid conversion with zero sales team is very capital efficient. The risk is classic SMB: high churn, low ACV, and the question of whether they can move upmarket. But Michael has a credible plan for a mid-market tier. I want to explore this.

- [ ] Sarah to review financial model and unit economics

title: Finley — Product Demo and Technical Review with Priya Anand (CTO)
author: James Morrison
content:
Meeting: Product demo and technical review — Finley
Date: February 20, 2026
Attendees: James Morrison (AIVC), Priya Anand (CTO, Finley)
Location: Zoom + screen share

## Summary

90-minute demo of the full product with Priya. The product is clean, intuitive, and surprisingly powerful for an SMB tool. Priya's Plaid background is evident in the data integration quality.

## Product Demo

- **Setup**: Connected a demo QuickBooks Online account. Within 3 minutes, Finley had pulled in all transactions, automatically categorized them, and generated a full P&L, balance sheet, and cash flow statement. The speed of setup is a key selling point — SMB owners have zero patience for complex onboarding.

- **Auto-Categorization**: AI correctly categorized 94% of transactions on first pass. The remaining 6% were flagged for review with suggested categories. As users correct categorizations, the model learns their preferences.

- **Financial Reports**: CFO-quality reports generated automatically. Comparable to what a $200/hour fractional CFO would produce. Reports include trend analysis, year-over-year comparisons, and plain-English commentary ("Revenue grew 12% MoM driven primarily by a 20% increase in subscription revenue").

- **AI Forecasting**: This is the standout feature. Finley builds 30/60/90-day forecasts for revenue, expenses, and cash position. Priya showed me backtested accuracy: within 8% of actuals on 90-day forecasts across their customer base. For comparison, most SMBs don't forecast at all, and those that do typically use linear extrapolation in Excel.

- **Insights Engine**: Proactive alerts — "Your accounts receivable aging increased by 15 days this month. Here are the 3 overdue invoices" or "At current burn rate, you have 8.2 months of runway." These are the kinds of insights an experienced CFO would surface.

## Technical Architecture

- **Data Layer**: Built on Plaid for bank feeds and direct API integrations with QBO, Xero, FreshBooks. Priya's Plaid experience shows — the data aggregation is rock-solid. Real-time sync (not batch).

- **AI Models**: Mix of classification models (transaction categorization), time-series forecasting (revenue/expense prediction), and LLM-based report generation (plain-English insights). Fine-tuned on SMB financial data.

- **Infrastructure**: Runs on AWS. SOC 2 Type II compliant (important for handling financial data). Bank-grade encryption at rest and in transit.

## Concerns

- **SMB Market Challenges**: High churn is the elephant in the room. SMBs go out of business, change tools frequently, and are price-sensitive. Finley's 4.5% monthly churn is better than SMB average (~6%) but still concerning.

- **ACV Ceiling**: At $6K/year average, there's limited room for expansion within the SMB segment. The mid-market tier ($25K ACV target for Q3) is critical to the business model.

## My Assessment

The product is genuinely good — it delivers real value to SMBs that would otherwise fly blind financially. Priya is a strong technical co-founder. The concern is entirely about the SMB business model dynamics, not the product itself.

## Action Items

- [ ] James to summarize product demo for Sarah
- [ ] Request data on churn cohort analysis (is churn business closure or product dissatisfaction?)
- [ ] Understand mid-market product roadmap in detail

title: Finley — Financial Deep-Dive with Michael Chang
author: Sarah Chen
content:
Meeting: Financial deep-dive — Finley
Date: March 10, 2026
Attendees: Sarah Chen (AIVC), Michael Chang (CEO)
Location: Zoom

## Summary

Detailed financial review. The product-led growth metrics are strong. The SMB churn is the main concern but Michael has a credible plan to address it.

## Financial Review

- **Revenue**: $1.9M ARR as of February 2026. Growing 18% quarter-over-quarter. Q4 2025 was $1.6M, Q3 2025 was $1.36M.

- **Customers**: 320 active. Segmentation: ~280 SMBs (1-50 employees), ~35 small mid-market (50-150 employees), ~5 larger mid-market (150-500 employees, on custom plans).

- **Average Contract Value**: $6K/year for self-serve SMB customers. $15K/year for the small mid-market cohort. $35K/year for the 5 larger accounts (these came through inbound, not self-serve).

- **Churn**: 4.5% monthly. Michael broke this down: roughly 60% of churned customers went out of business (normal SMB mortality), 25% switched to a competitor or back to spreadsheets, 15% outgrew Finley and moved to enterprise tools. The "outgrew" bucket is actually a good problem to have — it validates the mid-market opportunity.

- **Product-Led Growth**: 15% monthly conversion from free trial to paid. Trial-to-paid time: average 12 days. Customer acquisition cost: $1.8K (primarily content marketing and SEO). This is remarkably efficient.

- **LTV/CAC**: 3.2x. Below the 5x benchmark for SaaS but reasonable for SMB given the low CAC.

- **Margins**: Gross margins 80%. Low COGS — primarily cloud infrastructure and Plaid API costs.

- **Burn**: $210K/month. Lean operation. Runway: 14 months on existing cash ($2.9M remaining).

## Mid-Market Expansion Plan

- Michael plans to launch a mid-market tier in Q3 2026. Target: companies with 50-500 employees and finance teams of 1-5 people. ACV target: $25K/year.

- Features: multi-entity consolidation, team collaboration, approval workflows, custom dashboards, dedicated support. These are features the 5 existing larger customers have requested.

- Sales motion: hybrid. Product-led for onboarding, light-touch sales for expansion. Hiring 2 AEs focused on mid-market.

- This is critical to the investment thesis. If mid-market works, LTV improves dramatically and churn drops (mid-market companies have lower mortality than SMBs).

## Ribbit Capital Co-Lead

- Ribbit is offering $7M at $38M pre-money. They want one board seat. They'll be the fintech expertise partner.

- Ribbit wants AIVC specifically as co-lead because we bring AI/ML diligence capabilities and a portfolio of AI companies that could become Finley customers.

- Structure: $12M total. $7M Ribbit, $5M AIVC, $1.5M Kleiner follow-on, balance from existing angels.

## My Assessment

This is a bet on Michael's ability to navigate the SMB-to-mid-market transition. The product is strong, the PLG metrics are excellent, and the team is right. The SMB churn is a known risk with a credible mitigation plan. Ribbit's co-lead gives us fintech credibility and reduces our exposure ($5M vs full lead). I'm inclined to proceed.

## Action Items

- [ ] Sarah to prepare IC materials
- [ ] Build financial model with mid-market expansion scenarios
- [ ] Negotiate co-lead terms with Ribbit (board seat allocation, governance)
- [ ] Schedule IC presentation for early April

title: Finley — IC Presentation and Approval
author: Sarah Chen
content:
Meeting: Investment Committee — Finley Series A
Date: April 5, 2026
Attendees: Full AIVC team (Sarah Chen, David Okonkwo, Maya Patel, James Morrison, Elena Rodriguez)
Location: AIVC office, San Francisco

## Presentation Summary

Presented the Finley co-investment opportunity to IC.

**The Case FOR:**

- Market: SMB financial management is a $15B market. Still primarily spreadsheets — massive room for disruption. Mid-market expansion (50-500 employees) extends TAM significantly.

- Team: Michael Chang (ex-Stripe FP&A) + Priya Anand (ex-Plaid infrastructure). Michael knows what CFOs need because he was one. Priya can build the data infrastructure because she built Plaid's.

- PLG Metrics: 15% trial-to-paid conversion, $1.8K CAC, 12-day conversion time. This is a very efficient growth engine that doesn't require an expensive sales team.

- Product: James's demo confirmed it's genuinely useful. AI forecasting at 92% accuracy is impressive. Auto-categorization at 94% first-pass accuracy saves hours of manual work.

- Co-Lead: Ribbit Capital brings fintech credibility, banking relationships, and regulatory expertise. Reduces our risk — we're putting in $5M, not $12M.

**The Case AGAINST:**

- SMB churn: 4.5% monthly is high. Even with the business closure explanation, annual revenue churn is ~40%. Need mid-market to work.

- Low ACV: $6K/year limits revenue per customer. Mid-market tier ($25K ACV) needs to materialize.

- Competitive: Mosaic raised $40M, Datarails raised $50M — both better-funded and targeting overlapping markets (though more enterprise-focused).

- Small team: 26 employees, thin bench. Execution risk if they lose key people.

## Committee Discussion

- David: "SMB is hard. But the PLG metrics are legit and Michael's Stripe pedigree gives me confidence on the mid-market expansion. The co-lead structure makes this a reasonable risk."

- Maya: "The product is solid technically. Priya's Plaid background shows in the data layer. Concern is that AI forecasting accuracy will degrade as they move into different SMB verticals with different financial patterns."

- James: "Product demo was clean. The 3-minute setup from QBO connection to full financial dashboard is a compelling experience."

- Elena: "Market research confirms the opportunity. The competitors (Mosaic, Datarails, Jirav) are all going upmarket. Finley owns the SMB entry point."

## Decision

**APPROVED**: Co-lead Finley Series A with Ribbit Capital. $12M total round: $5M from AIVC, $7M from Ribbit, $1.5M Kleiner follow-on. $38M pre-money valuation. AIVC board observer seat. Ribbit board seat.

## Action Items

- [ ] Sarah to finalize co-lead terms with Ribbit
- [ ] Legal to review Ribbit's term sheet and prepare AIVC side letter
- [ ] Sarah to confirm terms with Michael
- [ ] Target closing by end of June

title: SMB Financial Planning Remains the Last Spreadsheet Frontier. AI Startups Want to Change That.
author: Daniel Webber
content:
SMB Financial Planning Remains the Last Spreadsheet Frontier. AI Startups Want to Change That.
By Daniel Webber | Fintech Futures | January 22, 2026

In an era where AI is transforming everything from customer support to software development, one corner of the business world remains stubbornly analog: small business financial planning.

According to a recent SCORE survey, 82% of small businesses with fewer than 50 employees still manage their financial planning primarily in spreadsheets. Only 11% use dedicated FP&A software — and most of those are using tools designed for enterprise companies that cost $50,000 or more per year.

The result is predictable: small businesses make critical financial decisions — hiring, inventory, expansion, pricing — based on stale data and rough calculations. Cash flow surprises remain the number one cause of SMB failure, ahead of market competition and product issues.

A new generation of AI-powered startups is targeting this gap. San Francisco-based Finley, founded by former Stripe Head of FP&A Michael Chang, offers an AI financial analyst that connects to accounting software and automatically generates reports, forecasts, and insights.

"I spent three years doing FP&A at Stripe with a team of 25 analysts and the best tools money can buy," Chang told Fintech Futures. "Then I'd talk to friends running small businesses and they were making million-dollar decisions based on a spreadsheet they updated once a month. The gap is absurd."

Finley says it has 320 SMB customers paying an average of $6,000 per year, with AI-generated forecasts that achieve 92% accuracy on 90-day predictions. The company uses a product-led growth model, converting 15% of free trial users to paid customers.

The market is attracting attention from several directions. Mosaic, which raised $40 million in Series B funding, targets mid-market and enterprise companies with strategic finance software. Datarails, backed by $50 million in Series B funding, automates FP&A for CFOs using Excel as the interface. Jirav offers budgeting and forecasting for SMBs but lacks the AI capabilities of newer entrants.

"The SMB financial planning market is large and underserved, but it's also notoriously difficult," cautioned Mercury CFO Ankur Nagpal. "High churn, low willingness to pay, and fierce competition from free spreadsheet tools. The winners will be companies that deliver so much value that the ROI is undeniable."

title: Mosaic Raises $40M Series B for Strategic Finance Platform
author: Mary Ann Azevedo
content:
Mosaic Raises $40M Series B for Strategic Finance Platform
By Mary Ann Azevedo | TechCrunch | February 8, 2026

Mosaic, the strategic finance platform for modern businesses, has raised $40 million in Series B funding led by General Catalyst with participation from Founders Fund, Lachy Groom, and existing investors.

The company, which was founded by former Palantir engineers, provides a financial planning and analysis platform that connects to a company's existing tech stack — ERP, CRM, HRIS, billing systems — to provide real-time financial metrics, budgeting, and forecasting. Unlike traditional FP&A tools that require months of implementation, Mosaic promises deployment in days.

"Strategic finance has been stuck in the dark ages," said Mosaic CEO Bijan Moallemi. "Finance teams spend 80% of their time collecting and organizing data, and only 20% analyzing it. We're flipping that ratio with automation and AI."

Mosaic focuses on mid-market and enterprise companies with 100-5,000 employees — the segment too large for basic tools like QuickBooks but not large enough for enterprise suites like Anaplan. The company says it has over 200 customers and grew revenue by 150% in 2025.

The fundraise comes as the FP&A automation market heats up. Datarails recently raised $50 million for its Excel-based FP&A platform, while newer entrants like Finley are targeting SMBs with AI-powered financial planning. The market is stratifying: enterprise (Anaplan, Adaptive Planning), mid-market (Mosaic, Datarails), and SMB (Finley, Jirav).

Moallemi acknowledged the competitive landscape but argued that market segmentation works in Mosaic's favor. "The mid-market has specific needs — they need ERP integrations that SMB tools don't support, but they don't need the complexity of enterprise platforms. We're purpose-built for that segment."

title: Datarails Raises $50M Series B for FP&A Automation, Targets CFOs
author: Alex Konrad
content:
Datarails Raises $50M Series B for FP&A Automation, Targets CFOs
By Alex Konrad | Forbes | March 15, 2026

Datarails, the financial planning and analysis platform that lets CFOs keep using Excel while automating the data infrastructure behind it, has raised $50 million in Series B funding led by ICONIQ Growth with participation from Zeev Ventures, Innovation Endeavors, and Vintage Investment Partners.

The New York and Tel Aviv-based company takes a deliberately contrarian approach to FP&A automation: rather than asking finance teams to abandon Excel — which most have invested years in mastering — Datarails plugs into existing Excel models and automates the manual data collection, consolidation, and reporting that eats up most of a finance team's time.

"CFOs don't want another platform to learn. They want their Excel to work better," said Datarails CEO Didi Gurfinkel. "We meet finance teams where they are. Our AI handles the data plumbing so CFOs can spend time on analysis and strategy."

Datarails claims over 800 customers, primarily in the 50-1,000 employee range, with annual contracts averaging $35,000. The company grew revenue by over 100% in 2025 and says it is approaching profitability.

The fundraise underscores growing investor appetite for tools that automate financial operations. The broader FP&A market is estimated at $8 billion, with automation penetration still below 20% for mid-market companies.

Competitors include Mosaic (strategic finance for mid-market), Anaplan and Adaptive Planning (enterprise), and newer AI-native startups like Finley (SMBs). The market appears large enough for multiple winners across different segments.

"What we're seeing is a generational shift in how companies manage their finances," said ICONIQ Growth partner Matthew Jacobson. "Every company needs FP&A automation — the question is which tool fits their size and sophistication level. Datarails is the clear leader for mid-market companies that live in Excel."
